blocks.text: **Microsoft Word** is Microsoft's **word-processing** application. You use it to create, edit, format, save and print documents such as letters, reports, resumes and study notes. It is one of the most widely used word processors in the world.

blocks.title: Key terms
rows: **What You See Is What You Get** - the editing screen closely matches the final printed page.
Press **Windows + R**, type **winword** and press Enter (Word must already be installed).
Word is a separate application. It is not automatically included with every Windows installation.

blocks.title: Development timeline
items: Original name
**Multi-Tool Word**
Key developers
**Charles Simonyi** and **Richard Brodie**
First release; early platforms included **Xenix** and **MS-DOS**
Macintosh version, with a graphical editing environment
**Word for Windows**
Word 2007 introduced the **Ribbon** user interface

blocks.title: Early and related names
items: **Electric Pencil** and **WordStar** were distinct early word processors. Electric Pencil is linked with the first word processor for microcomputers, but a question on the 'first word processor' needs a clearly defined category.
Apple's **Numbers** handles spreadsheets and **Keynote** handles presentations (Pages is the word processor).
**IBM** is the conventional exam answer for the company that introduced and popularised the term 'word processing'.

blocks.title: Quick recall
blocks.text: Word = word processing | Pages = Apple | 1983 = first release | 1989 = Word for Windows | 2007 = Ribbon.

blocks.title: Word window, top to bottom
items: Title bar + Quick Access
Document name, Save/Undo/Redo, window controls
Ribbon tabs and groups
File, Home, Insert, Draw, Design, Layout...
Ruler
Indents, tab stops, margin boundaries
Document area
Where text and objects are typed
Status bar
Page info, word count, view buttons, zoom slider

blocks.title: Top of the window
rows: Shows the **document name** and application information.
Sits at the **upper left** in Word 2007. Later versions use the File tab instead.
In the traditional layout it is to the right of the Office Button; the title text appears farther right.

blocks.text: The toolbar and the title text share the top area of the window - they are not separate, fixed side-by-side bars. Older Word versions used menus and toolbars; modern Word uses **tabs and command groups**. The tabs available and the number of 'bars' vary by version.

blocks.title: Quick Access Toolbar
items: A set of **customisable shortcuts** for frequent tasks.
Traditional default commands: **Save**, **Undo** and **Redo/Repeat**.
It can be moved or hidden, depending on the version and settings.

blocks.title: Editing area
rows: The workspace for text and objects.
The **blinking cursor** where new text appears.
Controls **indents, tab stops and margin boundaries**.
Moves the view up and down.
Moves the view left and right when required.

blocks.title: Bottom of the window
rows: Page information, **word count** and other indicators.
Normally at the **lower right**. Desktop zoom range is **10% - 500%**; **100%** is the normal reference magnification.

blocks.title: Ribbon tabs
items: Tabs: File, **Home**, Insert, Draw, Design, Layout, References, Mailings, Review, View, Help.
**Home** is the usual starting editing tab.
A document may reopen at its saved zoom, and zoom affects the **screen display only, not the printed size**.

blocks.title: Word file formats
rows: Rich Text Format - formatted text supported by several programs

items: A **template** is a reusable document starting point.
A **.docx** file does **not** store VBA macros; save macro-bearing documents as **.docm**.
**RTF** = Rich Text Format (extension .rtf).

blocks.title: WordPad, Notepad and Word
rows: A basic word processor bundled with older Windows releases. It was **removed from Windows 11 starting with version 24H2** and from **Windows Server 2025**.
A separate application, not included automatically with every Windows installation.

blocks.title: Recording a macro
items: Open the **View** tab.
Choose **Macros**, then **Record Macro**.
Perform the repeated steps (for example, a set of formatting steps).
Stop recording. Press **Alt + F8** at any time to open the Macros dialog.
Save the document as **.docm** so the macro is kept.

blocks.text: **Macros** automate repeated tasks through recorded or programmed commands. View Macros, Record and Pause Recording appear where supported.

blocks.title: Word + Excel: OLE
rows: Word is the **container/client**; Excel is the **source/server**.
Depend on which application **contains** the object.

blocks.title: Server roles
blocks.text: Typical servers host websites, share databases and handle email, so 'word processing' is the intended non-server role in the basic exam question. It is not an absolute restriction, though - servers can also provide document-processing services.

blocks.title: Clipboard and editing
rows: Redo or repeat a supported action

blocks.title: Copyright symbol
rows: **Ctrl + Alt + C** inserts the copyright symbol.

blocks.text: Unsaved changes normally trigger a save prompt when you close. Fields inserted by the date/time shortcuts can be updated. Custom keyboard settings can change any shortcut's behaviour.

blocks.title: Font basics
items: **Font face** = typeface, such as Arial, Cambria or Times New Roman.
Four common styles: **Regular, Italic, Bold, Bold Italic**. Regular is the usual body-text starting style.
Templates and user settings can change the default font.

blocks.title: Font size
items: Size range: **1 - 1,638 pt**, including half-point values.
Dropdown presets commonly run from **8 - 72 pt**.
Visible letter height also depends on the typeface.

blocks.title: Font effects
rows: Smaller raised text, as in x2.
Smaller lowered text, as in H2O.
Lowercase letters appear as small capitals.

blocks.title: Change Case - five options (example: Banking exams need practice.)

blocks.text: **Shift + F3** cycles through the common case forms, but it does not cycle through all five options in the Change Case menu.

blocks.title: Four paragraph alignments
rows: Lines align with the left margin (usual for English body text)
Text is centred between the margins
Lines align with the right margin
Spacing aligns most lines with both margins; the last line usually stays left-aligned

blocks.text: **Ctrl + Q** removes direct paragraph formatting and restores the settings of the paragraph style.

blocks.title: Three different breaks
rows: Line break within the same paragraph

blocks.title: F8 Extend Selection (starting with no selection)
items: Press **F8** once to activate Extend Selection.
Press F8 twice to select the current **word**.
Press F8 three times to select the current **sentence**.
Press **Esc** to exit Extend Selection mode.

blocks.title: Proofing marks
rows: **Contextual** spelling (a correctly spelled word used incorrectly).
Commonly **red for spelling**, **blue for grammar**, and other colours for refinements.

blocks.title: Word Count
items: Counts **pages, words, characters (with and without spaces), paragraphs and lines**.
It can include **text boxes, footnotes and endnotes**.
Modern path: **Review > Word Count**; older versions used the **Tools** menu.
A **dictionary** primarily supplies definitions, while a thesaurus gives synonyms.

blocks.title: Orientation and paper size
rows: **Taller than wide**; the usual blank-page orientation.
**Layout > Orientation** (older tab: Page Layout). **Layout > Size** selects paper dimensions.
**8.5 x 11 inches** - the exam answer for US-style defaults.

blocks.text: Actual defaults depend on the region, template and printer.

items: Margins separate body content from the page edges. The four sides are **Top, Bottom, Left and Right** - 'Centre' is an alignment, not a margin side.
1 inch = 2.54 cm. Defaults can be changed; use **Layout > Margins > Custom Margins**.
**Gutter** = extra space at the **binding edge**, so text is not hidden by a book's spine. Its position depends on binding and page settings.

blocks.title: Header and footer
rows: Titles, dates, page numbers or organisation details.
They can repeat, with different first-page, odd/even or section settings.

blocks.title: Print settings
rows: The page that contains the cursor
Specified pages/ranges - for example '2, 5-8' prints page 2 and pages 5 to 8

blocks.title: Save choices
rows: Saves under **another name, location or format**.

blocks.title: Home tab groups
rows: Name, style, effects, colour, size; Bold, Italic, Underline and Font Colour belong here
Alignment, lists, indentation, spacing and paragraph controls

items: **Format Painter** copies **formatting**, not the text itself.
The Font dialog shows name, style, effects, colour, size and a preview; the Paragraph dialog has **Indents and Spacing** and **Line and Page Breaks** tabs.
Clipboard, Font and Paragraph are **groups**, not single commands.

blocks.title: Insert tab groups
rows: Cover Page, Blank Page, Page Break
Pictures, Shapes, Icons, SmartArt, 3D Models, Chart, Screenshot
Text Box, Quick Parts, WordArt, **Drop Cap**

items: **Drop Cap** enlarges a paragraph's opening letter across several lines.
**Styles** primarily belong to the **Home** tab, not Insert.
Older Insert tabs included **Clip Art**.

blocks.title: Draw tab
rows: Offers ruled/grid backgrounds in supported builds.

blocks.text: Drawing tools vary by Word version and device.

blocks.title: Layout tab - Page Setup
rows: Letter, Tabloid, Legal, Statement, Executive, A3, A4, A5, B4, B5 (choices can depend on printer support).
Controls word division at line ends.

blocks.title: Layout tab - Arrange objects
rows: Locate an object on the page.
Control text flow around an object.

blocks.title: Layout tab - Paragraph and the Ruler
items: The Layout Paragraph group adjusts **left/right indents** and **spacing before/after** paragraphs; the Paragraph dialog also holds Line and Page Breaks settings.
The **ruler** adjusts first-line and hanging indents, tab stops and margin boundaries in suitable views. It changes layout/formatting rather than rewriting the text.

blocks.text: **Design** controls the coordinated look (themes, colours, fonts, page background). **Layout** controls page geometry, paragraph placement and object arrangement. Command positions can vary by release.

blocks.title: References tab
rows: Insert and update a heading-based contents list.
Insert explanatory notes and move to the next note.
Research assistance where available (tools changed across versions).
Label tables, figures and other objects.

blocks.text: Table of Contents, Footnotes and Citations & Bibliography are all groups on the References tab.

**Mail Merge** produces many personalised documents from one common document and a recipient list. For example, the same invitation can carry a different name and address for every recipient. Outputs include letters, envelopes, labels and email messages.

blocks.title: Mailings tab workflow
items: Start Mail Merge
Choose the document type
Select Recipients
Choose the data source
Edit Recipient List
Filter or adjust recipients
Write & Insert Fields
Add recipient information
Preview Results
Check each personalised version
Finish & Merge
Produce, print or send
The Mailings tab also has a **Create** group with **Envelopes and Labels**.
Mailings is specialised for correspondence and bulk personalisation.

blocks.title: 'Least used tab' questions
blocks.text: No Ribbon tab is universally the 'least used'. Someone who prepares many personalised letters may use Mailings very often - usage depends on the person's work, not on a fixed Word rule.

blocks.title: Review tab
rows: Identifies barriers for readers with disabilities.

blocks.title: View tab
rows: Read Mode, Print Layout, Web Layout, Outline, Draft.
New Window, Arrange All, Split, Switch Windows.
View, Record and Pause Recording where available.

blocks.title: Five traditional views
rows: Page boundaries, margins, headers/footers - how it will print

blocks.text: **Properties** is not a universal View command - document properties are commonly found under **File > Info**.

blocks.title: AI in Word
rows: Can assist with drafting, rewriting and summarising in supported editions/subscriptions.
A Microsoft digital assistant, **not** Word's former built-in AI. Cortana has been retired.
Depends on version, device and subscription.

sections.title: File Tab, Borders, Clip Art and Exam Distinctions

blocks.title: Word 2007 Office Button
items: An upper-left button containing **New, Open, Save, Save As, Print, Prepare, Send, Publish and Close**.
Prepare, Send and Publish were all present in it.
Later versions use the **File** tab instead.

blocks.title: Borders
items: Borders can surround **pages, text, paragraphs, pictures and tables**; you choose the line style, colour and thickness.
Page borders: **Design > Page Borders** (older versions may use Page Layout).
**Art** provides decorative page-border graphics.
A picture border frames a picture; a text border frames selected text. 'Colourful, text, picture' describe different border aspects/targets, not three equal page-border categories.

blocks.title: Clip art and pictures
items: Older Word
Included a dedicated **Clip Art** command (ready-made illustrations).
Microsoft announced the closure of the **Office.com Clip Art** and image library.
Afterwards
**Bing Image Search** became an alternative; existing saved illustrations could still be inserted.

blocks.text: The closure of the Office.com Clip Art library did not remove all illustration support from Word.

blocks.title: Final exam distinctions
items: A Word **table** allows **63 columns**; text-layout columns are a different feature.
To **split a table**, place the cursor in the row that will start the new table, then press **Ctrl + Shift + Enter**.
'Paint-style Brush' is not a standard Word text-editing command. **Format Painter** has a brush icon; supported Word versions also offer pens/drawing tools.
Version-specific questions need version-specific answers.

revision: Word is a word processor; WYSIWYG = What You See Is What You Get; open it with Windows + R, then winword.
Original name Multi-Tool Word; developers Charles Simonyi and Richard Brodie; first release 1983; Word for Windows 1989; Ribbon from Word 2007.
.doc = old format, .docx = standard since 2007 (no macros), .docm = macro-enabled, .dotx = template, .dotm = macro template, .rtf = Rich Text Format.
OLE = Object Linking and Embedding; Word is the container/client and Excel the source/server when an Excel object sits in Word.
Alt + F8 opens the Macros dialog; macros are recorded from View > Macros > Record Macro; save as .docm.
Ctrl+N new, Ctrl+O open, Ctrl+S save, Ctrl+P print, Ctrl+W close, Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+Y redo, Ctrl+A select all, Ctrl+F find, Ctrl+H replace, Ctrl+K hyperlink.
Alignment shortcuts: Ctrl+L left, Ctrl+E centre, Ctrl+R right, Ctrl+J justify; Ctrl+Q resets paragraph formatting.
Enter = paragraph break; Shift+Enter = line break; Ctrl+Enter = page break.
F7 = spelling/grammar; Shift+F7 = Thesaurus; Ctrl+Shift+G = Word Count; F8 pressed twice selects a word, three times a sentence.
Font size range 1 - 1,638 pt; 72 pt = 1 inch; defaults: Times New Roman 12 (2003), Calibri 11 (2007-2021), Aptos (newer 365).
Margins: 1 inch on all sides from Word 2007; older Word had 1.25 inch left/right. Letter = 8.5 x 11 in; A4 = 210 x 297 mm.
Mail merge parts: main document, data source, merge fields; steps on the Mailings tab end with Finish & Merge.
Desktop zoom range is 10% - 500%; zoom changes the screen display, not the printed size.
Five traditional views: Print Layout, Read Mode, Web Layout, Outline, Draft; a Word table allows 63 columns; Ctrl+Shift+Enter splits a table.
